title: Phrasal Verbs with Get
intro: In this section you will learn useful phrasal verbs with get in English.

meanings: To travel and visit places frequently.
To move around actively.
To spread information or rumors.
items.example: It's easy to get about the city by bike.

meanings: To convey an opinion successfully.
To move from one place to another.
items.example: It's hard to get my ideas across in English.

items.es: perseguir; insistir a alguien (para que haga algo)
meanings: To chase or catch someone or something.
To make someone do something.
items.example: The cat got after the mouse.

meanings: To succeed in your endeavors.
items.example: You need to work hard to get ahead.

meanings: To have a healthy relationship with someone else.
To leave.
To cope with a situation.
items.example: My brother and I get along well.

meanings: To travel frequently to different places.
To physically move around.
To overcome a problem.
items.example: Grandpa uses a wheelchair to get around.

meanings: To imply something.
To reach or obtain something.
items.example: What are you getting at?

meanings: To return to a previous location.
items.example: What time did you get back home?

meanings: To seek revenge against someone or something.
items.example: She wants to get back at him for the joke.

meanings: To support someone or something.
To be late in something; not keeping up with something.
items.example: The whole town got behind the local team.

meanings: To be able to cope with a particular situation.
items.example: I can get by with a little Spanish.

meanings: To leave a vehicle.
To make someone depressed.
items.example: Get down from that tree!

meanings: To write notes or information.
items.example: Wait, let me get your address down.

items.es: entrar; subir (a un vehículo); ser admitido
meanings: When you enter a place or a vehicle.
When you get admitted to an institution.
items.example: Get in, I'll drive you home.

meanings: When you become interested in something.
To enter a vehicle.
items.example: I got into photography last year.

meanings: To leave a vehicle or transport.
items.example: We get off the bus at the next stop.

meanings: To enter a vehicle or transport.
To make progress in something.
items.example: Get on the train quickly!

items.es: llevarse bien con; seguir con (una tarea)
meanings: To have a good relationship with someone.
To start or continue to do a task.
items.example: Stop talking and get on with your work.

meanings: To leave a place in a hurry.
When something is revealed.
items.example: Get out of the house: it's on fire!

meanings: To recover from a difficult situation.
items.example: It took him a year to get over the breakup.

meanings: To have a good relationship with someone else.
items.example: I get along with my neighbors.

meanings: To escape from somewhere.
items.example: The thief got away.

items.es: salirse con la suya, quedar impune
meanings: To do something illicit and not get caught.
items.example: He cheated on the test and got away with it.

meanings: To lose control over something because you are very excited.
items.example: I got carried away and bought too many shoes.

meanings: To dispose of someone or something that is not needed anymore.
items.example: I need to get rid of these old clothes.

meanings: To meet with people for a specific event.
items.example: Let's get together this weekend.

meanings: To rise from a lying or sitting position.
items.example: I get up at seven every day.
